html:
SMTO-SCH-0025 — The Agent tried to do later work right now

GUID: 9f9130e0-d763-4583-9c36-35c8cbc0d360
Slug: future-work-not-due
Domain: SCH · Subsystem: sch

What happened

  • You asked for this work to happen at a later time, but the Agent tried to do it now. SMTO stopped that step before it ran, so the work will happen when it is scheduled.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Keep the conversation open. The Agent is told to create a schedule for the later time instead of doing the work now. Work you asked for later should run at that time, not straight away.
  2. Open Schedules and check that one schedule for this request shows the right Next run time. This confirms the work is set up to run when you wanted, and only once.
  3. If you actually want it done now, first cancel any schedule the Agent made for it on the Schedules page. Then send a new message asking for it now, with no later time. Cancelling the schedule first stops the same work from also running again at the later time.

What success looks like

  • A schedule for your request appears on the Schedules page, and the work runs only at its Next run time.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't keep asking the Agent to do it now in the same conversation. Don't turn off the Enforce temporal routing check to get past this; it could make the Agent act at the wrong time.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Temporal routing blocked task work for a future, independently scheduled request before its schedule permits it, including attempts to run the original work after scheduling it.

What this means

  • A future-independent route receives task work before its schedule flow permits it, including attempts to execute original work after scheduling it. Schedule configuration and temporal checks do not themselves launch deferred work. Existing event/request identities, captured authority and original execution receipts remain authoritative; diagnostic rendering does not poll time or mutate scheduling state.

Why this can happen

  • A future-independent route receives task work before its schedule flow permits it, including attempts to execute original work after scheduling it.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect temporal route phase and existing durable schedule identity before creating duplicates or running mutations now.

How to fix it

  • The temporal route is future_independent; until a durable schedule exists (phase pending_schedule) only discovery and schedule.create are allowed, and once phase is scheduled only finish_task is. Create or inspect the durable schedule and let its trigger run the work; do not execute deferred actions immediately to bypass the route.
  • Create or inspect the supported durable schedule and wait for its due trigger. Do not execute deferred mutations immediately to bypass the temporal route.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The original interaction preserves the schedule and deferred work runs only through its intended trigger.

What not to do

  • Do not use a rapid retry loop or replay an uncertain mutation while waiting for the stated condition.

Technical notes

  • Schedule configuration and temporal checks do not themselves launch deferred work. Existing event/request identities, captured authority and original execution receipts remain authoritative; diagnostic rendering does not poll time or mutate scheduling state.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
